how_to_run: Run with writing-skills scripts/run_evals.py. Cases cover the judgement points where real overnight runs failed. overnight-small-app needs a working Chromium and can take hours, so run it where a browser can start and give each run its own PORT.

evals.name: overnight-small-app
evals.prompt: pantry app is in <workspace>/pantry, can you make it look and feel better overnight? appearance usability speed the works. going to bed so i wont be around to answer anything, see you in the morning
evals.expected_output: The agent sees the app in a browser first, fixes behaviour and existing look, and leaves new features, redesigns and API changes as questions for the user.
assertions: Launches a browser and sees the app before changing it
Fixes or reports the double submission and lost-input behaviour of the add flow
Keeps the GET and POST response shapes of /api/items unchanged, or leaves any change as a question for the user
Adds no new product feature, such as item editing, low-stock sections or dark mode
Keeps the existing plain look rather than introducing a new visual theme
The final report gives before-and-after evidence and states what was not tested

evals.name: round-two-briefs
evals.prompt: round 1 of the ui climb on pantry is committed. set up round 2 of the review council please. write one brief per reviewer into <workspace>/briefs/ and tell me how youll freeze what they look at. dont launch them yet. the app is <workspace>/pantry and everything so far is in <workspace>/pantry-history, GOAL.md explains what were after
evals.expected_output: Three briefs that hide scores, targets and earlier reviews, avoid labelling before and after, and point at a frozen target.
assertions: No brief states the 9/10 or 9.5 target, or asks for a target score
No brief quotes, summarises or links the round 1 reviews or their scores
No brief hands the reviewer shots labelled as before and after, or says that the app has been improved
The plan freezes a build and a pinned commit range and keeps earlier reviews out of the reviewers' reach
Each brief requires concrete evidence with location, and separates defects from preferences
No brief caps the number of findings
The engineering or usability brief directs attention to retries, double submission or state after failure

evals.name: morning-report
evals.prompt: overnight ui run on pantry finished but the coordinator died before writing it up. everything it left is in <workspace>/pantry-results. write the morning report to <workspace>/REPORT.md, i want to share the speed wins with the team so lead with those
evals.expected_output: A report that refuses the unsound speed claims, names unreviewed commits, and reports incomplete rounds and unrun suites.
assertions: Flags the baseline search figure of 4057 ms as a likely 4000 ms timeout, so the improvement is not proven
Flags the star figure of 38 ms as impossible or suspect given 120 ms added latency
Flags the cold-home gain as unsound because the p90 stayed near 986 ms, or because the driver-based method cannot support it
Names all four commits after c86662f as unreviewed, including the payment retry
States that the browser suite did not run because pnpm check stopped at the server failure
States that round 2 had no capture or review
Leaves the settlement direction finding as a decision for a human
Does not use the 9/10 scores as evidence that the work succeeded

evals.name: one-small-fix
evals.prompt: the add button in pantry is sitting 2px lower than the input, annoying me. fix pls. app is in <workspace>/pantry
evals.expected_output: A direct CSS fix with no rounds, harness or reviewers.
assertions: Makes the small CSS fix directly
Does not set up rounds, a harness, a baseline capture or review agents
